statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-109476 (GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8) is an ASP.NET Core information disclosure: a crafted X-Forwarded-Prefix header can inject cookie path delimiters, because cookie paths derived from PathBase did not percent-encode semicolons. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 10.0.15 and lists the ASP.NET Core runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, from 10.0.0 through 10.0.14 as affected (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/508, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.15/10.0.15.md). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 10.0.15-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v10.0.115 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v10.0.115). Scanned all 154 packages of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives: every build ships an ASP.NET Core shared framework from its own .NET release, in the ASP.NET Core shared framework of aspnetcore10-runtime and in the SDK, runtime-pack nupkg and ASP.NET Core runtime archive held by dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap; the earlier builds carry 10.0.8 through 10.0.14 and 10.0.15-r0 carries 10.0.15 on both architectures. The range ends at 10.0.15-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109476 (GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8) is an ASP.NET Core information disclosure issue: a crafted X-Forwarded-Prefix header can inject cookie path delimiters, because cookie paths derived from PathBase did not percent-encode semicolons; the fix covers ASP.NET Core authentication cookies, antiforgery and MVC temp data, and adds a shared CookiePathEscaper helper (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/7ce5a6b05d4d6694bb688bf7053ebb594c00a8e5). Microsoft lists the ASP.NET Core 8.0 runtime packs, including linux-musl-x64 and linux-musl-arm64, as affected from 8.0.0-rc.1 up to 8.0.33 and fixed in 8.0.34 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/508, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). DHI dotnet8-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 8 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries; 8.0.34-r0 is built from the dotnet/dotnet v8.0.134 source tag (https://github.com/dotnet/dotnet/releases/tag/v8.0.134), and its ASP.NET Core assemblies record the dotnet/aspnetcore v8.0.34 commit, e74b08d, which contains the fix commit (the v8.0.33 tag does not). In aspnetcore8-runtime of all ten published builds (8.0.23-r0, 8.0.24-r0, 8.0.25-r0, 8.0.26-r0, 8.0.27-r0, 8.0.29-r0, 8.0.31-r0, 8.0.32-r0, 8.0.33-r0 and 8.0.34-r0), for x86_64 and aarch64, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.dll, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures.dll carry the build's own ASP.NET Core version; the 8.0.34-r0 copies contain the CookiePathEscaper type and the copies in the earlier builds do not. dotnet8-runtime-bootstrap in each of those builds, on both architectures, also holds the ASP.NET Core shared framework and the ASP.NET Core runtime pack, extracted and as a NuGet package, at the build's own version: 8.0.23 through 8.0.33 in the earlier builds and 8.0.34 in 8.0.34-r0. The range ends at 8.0.34-r0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109476 (GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8) is an ASP.NET Core information disclosure: a crafted X-Forwarded-Prefix header can inject cookie path delimiters, because cookie paths derived from PathBase did not percent-encode semicolons. Microsoft fixed it in ASP.NET Core 8.0.34 (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/508, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/8.0/8.0.34/8.0.34.md). The fix is in the ASP.NET Core authentication, antiforgery and MVC cookie code, which ships in the ASP.NET Core shared framework. DHI dotnet-sdk-8 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK, and the .NET 8.0.34 release notes name .NET SDK 8.0.428 as part of that release. Read the file list of every published dotnet-sdk-8 build for amd64 and arm64: each holds exactly one ASP.NET Core shared framework, under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, plus reference assemblies under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, and the dotnet-sdk-8-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. The affected builds, with the ASP.NET Core runtime each holds: 8.0.422-0 holds 8.0.28; 8.0.423-0 and 8.0.423-1 hold 8.0.29; 8.0.424-1 holds 8.0.30; 8.0.425-0 and 8.0.425-1 hold 8.0.31; 8.0.426-0 holds 8.0.32; 8.0.427-0 holds 8.0.33. The first build of SDK 8.0.428, 8.0.428-0, and the current 8.0.428-1 hold ASP.NET Core 8.0.34 on both architectures. The 8.0 fix, https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/7ce5a6b05d4d6694bb688bf7053ebb594c00a8e5, adds a CookiePathEscaper used by the authentication, antiforgery and MVC TempData cookie code. In 8.0.428-0 on both architectures, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.dll, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures.dll in the shared framework report product version 8.0.34+e74b08d77b0c6e9f5d3a99cc2a3807a495f48db3, the v8.0.34 commit of dotnet/aspnetcore, which contains the fix, and contain CookiePathEscaper; the 8.0.33 copies in 8.0.427-0 report the v8.0.33 commit, which does not, and lack it. The range ends at 8.0.428-0 because it is the first published build with the fix.

CVE-2026-109476 (GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8) is an ASP.NET Core information disclosure: a crafted X-Forwarded-Prefix header can inject cookie path delimiters, because cookie paths derived from PathBase did not percent-encode semicolons. Microsoft lists the Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime 9.0 packages up to 9.0.22 as affected and fixed it in ASP.NET Core 9.0.23 with https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/commit/1fa5639647ddd2061bafe2ccf60bdc1c345b0b34, which adds a CookiePathEscaper used by the authentication, antiforgery and MVC TempData cookie code (https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/security/advisories/GHSA-xhj5-c3g8-pfj8, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/508). DHI dotnet-sdk-9 for Debian 13 repackages Microsoft's .NET SDK, and the .NET 9.0.23 release notes ship SDK 9.0.321 with the 9.0.23 runtimes (https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.23/9.0.23.md). Every published dotnet-sdk-9 build for amd64 and arm64 holds one .NET runtime under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.NETCore.App/<version> and one ASP.NET Core shared framework under /usr/lib/dotnet/shared/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App/<version>, at the same version; the dotnet-sdk-9-oci-config package from the same source holds only a configuration file and its changelog. Builds 9.0.315-0 to 9.0.320-0 (9.0.315-0, 9.0.316-0, 9.0.316-1, 9.0.317-1, 9.0.318-0, 9.0.318-1, 9.0.319-0, 9.0.320-0) hold 9.0.17 to 9.0.22; 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1 hold 9.0.23. In 9.0.321-0 and 9.0.321-1 on both architectures, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.dll, Microsoft.AspNetCore.Antiforgery.dll and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.ViewFeatures.dll in the 9.0.23 shared framework contain CookiePathEscaper, which the 9.0.22 copies in 9.0.320-0 lack; the only other copies of those assemblies in those builds are the reference assemblies under /usr/lib/dotnet/packs/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Ref, and none sits inside the bundled .nupkg or .zip archives. The range ends at 9.0.321-0, the first published build with the fix.
